catalog_quote: Ударение у именных частей речи, как правило, падает на последний слог слова: dasté 'рукоятка', mɛrkeyín 'мужчина', kuté 'дитя', γašang 'красивый'. С присоединением к слову каких-л. суффиксальных элементов ударение переходит на них: mɛrkeyinún 'мужчины', kåtún 'дети', γašangtár 'красивее'. Не принимают на себя ударение: 1) окончание косвенного падежа -i: Hasáni kɛtåb 'книга Хасана', kåtúni kɛtåb 'книга детей'; 2) неопределенный (выделительный) артикль -i: mɛrkeyín-i boya 'был один мужчина'; 3) послелоги dɛ, re, mu. У глаголов в прошедшем времени ударение сохраняется на последнем слоге основы: våporsíyi 'я спросил', våporsíyun 'мы спросили'; в формах настоящего времени изъявительного и сослагательного наклонений ударение переходит на окончание: våporsɛndí 'я спрашиваю', våporsɛnún 'мы спрашиваем', våporsún '(если) я спрошу'. new_statements.quote: § 29. Les règles de l'accentuation en sängesārī ne diffèrent guère de celles du sourkhéï et du lāsguerdī sauf sur un seul point: en général les préfixes neutres et les préfixes conjugatifs des verbes n'ont pas d'accent. A l'impératif, cependant, le préfixe bä, be etc. et les préfixes neutres sont souvent accentués. Le préfixe négatif porte toujours l'accent, ou l'accent principal, si un accent secondaire repose sur le thème ou la désinence. [p. 100] — [The rule referred to, p. 34, § 35, on Sourkhéï and Läsguerdī:] Pour l'accentuation, les deux patois suivent en général les mêmes règles que le persan.
new_statements.translation: § 29. The rules of accentuation in Sängesārī hardly differ from those of Sourkhéï and Lāsguerdī except on a single point: in general the neutral prefixes and the conjugational prefixes of verbs bear no accent. In the imperative, however, the prefix bä, be etc. and the neutral prefixes are often accented. The negative prefix always bears the accent, or the main accent if a secondary accent rests on the stem or the ending. [p. 100] — [p. 34, § 35:] As regards accentuation, the two dialects in general follow the same rules as Persian.
new_statements.citation: Christensen, Arthur. 1935. Contributions à la dialectologie iranienne. II. Dialectes de la région de Sèmnân: Sourkhéï, Läsguerdī, Sängesärī et Chämerzådī. Det Kgl. Danske Videnskabernes Selskab, Historisk-filologiske Meddelelser XXI, 3. København: Levin & Munksgaard.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Christensen gives no direct nominal rule for Sangesari; he states that its stress rules are those of Sourkhei/Lasgerdi, which 'in general follow the same rules as Persian' — i.e. the Persian pattern of word-final stress on nouns and adjectives, with morphologically governed stress in the verb: in unprefixed verb forms the preterite stresses the stem and the present the ending (§ 36, stated for Sourkhei); in Sangesari the verbal (neutral and conjugational) prefixes are unstressed, except that in the imperative the prefix bä/be etc. and the neutral prefixes are often stressed; the negative prefix always takes the (main) stress. The 'final' reading is thus inherited by reference to Persian rather than stated in so many words.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Mentioned: when the negative prefix carries the main accent, a secondary accent may rest on the verb stem or the ending (§ 29). For Sourkhei/Lasgerdi (§ 36-37) the ending can carry a secondary accent in the preterite and after a stressed prefix, sometimes almost as strong as the prefix accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Verbal prefixes (neutral and conjugational) normally unstressed in Sangesari, unlike Sourkhei/Lasgerdi where prefixes attract the main stress; imperative prefixes often stressed; negative prefix always stressed. For the sister dialects (§ 38) the ezafe -e, conjunctions, the relative pronoun, prepositions and postpositions are unstressed; § 31 notes prefix vocalism (ba- vs bo-) depends on whether the prefix/ending or the stem is stressed. Author notes his Sangesari material is scanty ('le peu de matériaux dont je dispose').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation and paradigm forms, mainly verb morphology; nominal stress only by reference to Persian. Data partly from an anonymous informant of 1914 (marked '1914') plus later material; no instrumental or phrase-level account.
new_statements.identity_note: Christensen 1935 describes the 'dialecte de Sängesär' (the town of Sangesar, today Mahdishahr, Semnan province), i.e. sang1315 itself, not a differently named variety; material is limited (partly one anonymous informant of 1914). His sister dialects Sourkhéï (sorkhei) and Läsguerdī (lasgerdi) are the reference point for the rule, and Persian is the reference point for theirs.
